pairs.question: Ast ego cui sacrae Caesar nova gaudia cenae nunc primum dominaque dedit consurgere mensa, qua celebrem mea vota lyra, quas solvere grates sufficiam?
pairs.answer: Non, si pariter mihi vertice laeto nectat odoratas et Smyrna et Mantua lauros, digna loquar.
pairs.derivation: Authorial rhetorical question and its self-answer. The setup 'ast ego cui... consurgere mensa' is kept verbatim so 'vota'/'grates' have a referent (the honor of Caesar's banquet). Question ends at the '?' after 'sufficiam'. Answer is the contiguous sentence from line 67 'non' through line 69 'digna loquar.', stopping at the first full stop; what follows ('mediis videor discumbere in astris...') turns to describing the banquet and does not answer the question. Inline verse numbers (5, 10) stripped; 'Non' capitalized as sentence start.

pairs.question: Quis duri silicis gravisque ferri immanis sonus aequori propinquum saxosae latus Appiae replevit?
pairs.answer: Sed qui limina bellicosa Iani iustis legibus et foro coronat, quis castae Cereri diu negata reddit iugera sobriasque terras, quis fortem vetat interire sexum et censor prohibet mares adultos pulchrae supplicium timere formae; qui reddit Capitolio Tonantem et Pacem propria domo reponit, qui genti patriae futura semper sancit lumina Flaviumque caelum, hic segnis populi vias gravatus et campos iter omne detinentes longos eximit ambitus novoque iniectu solidat graves harenas.
pairs.derivation: Authorial rhetorical question (what made this enormous sound of flint and iron along the Appian Way?) answered by the poet. The reply opens with a non-answering preamble 'certe non Libycae sonant catervae, nec dux advena... nec frangit vada... Nero sordidas paludes;' (lines 133-137) listing what it is NOT, so the answer's start is advanced past the semicolon to the operative answering span beginning 'sed qui limina bellicosa Iani...' (line 138). The span is contiguous and grammatically complete: the long relative chain resolves in 'hic... longos eximit ambitus novoque iniectu solidat graves harenas' = the emperor who builds the road. Answer cut at the full stop after 'graves harenas' (line 152, 'harenas,' normalized to 'harenas.'); what follows ('gaudens Euboicae domum Sibyllae...') is participial digression praising the road's reach. Inline verse numbers (5,10,15,20) stripped.
